name: Isar
tagline: Fast Flutter/Dart object database with rich indexed queries, now stalled upstream.
description: Isar is a cross-platform embedded database for Flutter, written in Rust with a Dart API. Collections are annotated Dart classes, and you get composite and multi-entry indexes, full-text word indexes, links between objects, ACID transactions and a type-safe generated query builder. It became the most popular Flutter-native database after Hive. Upstream development has stalled: the last stable release is 3.1.0 from April 2023, and the announced 4.0 rewrite never shipped. Most active users now depend on the community fork isar_community or have moved to ObjectBox, Drift or Hive CE.
statusNote: No stable release since 3.1.0 (April 2023) and the 4.0 rewrite never shipped; the community fork isar_community carries ongoing fixes.
developer: Simon Choi and the Isar community
strengths: Type-safe, code-generated queries with composite and multi-entry indexes
Fast native core in Rust with async APIs that keep the UI thread free
Watchers make it easy to build reactive Flutter widgets
Built-in inspector for browsing data during development
weaknesses: Upstream is effectively stalled; long-term maintenance depends on a community fork
useCases: Existing Flutter apps already built on Isar
Local caches and offline data for Flutter mobile apps
notIdealFor: New long-lived projects that need an active upstream
Apps needing sync out of the box
